title: South Korea and Taiwan overtake Japan in first-half exports on AI chip boom
summary: First-half figures are dollar-denominated and price-driven — high-bandwidth memory and Taiwan-packaged chips for Nvidia lifted Korea and Taiwan while Japan's upstream tools missed the surge, leaving the lead fragile to currencies, tariffs and a potential supply glut after 2028.

claims.text: Japanese government (METI) counters H1 ranking narrative with national semiconductor strategy centered on Rapidus: additional 5631.5bn (~$4.0bn) support for FY2026 decided April 11, bringing cumulative R&D support to 2.354tn (~$14.8bn), targeting 2nm mass production in H2 FY2027 at Chitose, Hokkaido, with METI Minister Ryosei Akazawa pledging 'spare no necessary support'. Primary METI action; steelmans Japanese official pushback that H1 gap reflects upstream positioning while Tokyo funds finished-chip catch-up.

claims.text: Rapidus governance shifted from grants to direct state ownership: 150bn equity via IPA (June 2026), golden share veto for METI, projected total gov support >3tn (~$18.8bn) by end FY2027 vs 167.6bn private from 32 firms; analysts skeptical  Semiecosystem Mark LaPedus estimates 5% probability of high-volume 2nm by 2027, 65-70% still in R&D, with funding gap to 5-7tn needed for stable production and TSMC/Samsung already in 2nm volume late 2025.

claims.text: H1 overtaking is dollar-denominated, price- and FX-driven half-year reading, not volume: Japan June 2026 exports +19.3% YoY by value but volumes +0.2% only, per Capital Economics Marcel Thieliant, reflecting yen at ~163/dollar and soaring memory prices (semiconductor shipments +53.8%); won/NT$ also weak, but price effect dominates, and Japan's export quantity index flat since pre-2008.

claims.text: H1 2026 simultaneous overtaking does not yet equal full-year regime change: full-year 2025 Japan still ahead of Korea by ~$29bn (and 6th globally), H1 is seasonally volatile, and Japan rebounded strongly in June (+19.3%) on semiconductor equipment to Taiwan (+46.4%) and China (+17.6%); whether H2 seasonality, yen moves, and US tariff effects (15% on Japan) narrow gap remains open.
